# EnterpriseGlue v0.29.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.28.13`.

## Highlights

- **managed Cloud account authentication:** Allow a new managed Cloud user to verify an email address and register a passkey without granting organization access from the address alone.

## User and administrator impact

- New Cloud users can choose an email and passkey sign-up path separate from federated sign-in.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Deploy the signed schema-epoch compatibility release and verify its exact 0131 dual-context ledger. Drain old tenant-GUC consumers, then use the separately credentialed passkey owner to apply and verify 0132 explicit-context enforcement before applying 0133 and enabling the new flow.

## API and integration compatibility

- Add Cloud email-signup verification and passkey registration and authentication endpoints.

## Configuration

- Managed Cloud account identity and a working global outbound email configuration are required; the relying-party origin is the configured frontend origin.

## Database migrations

- Migration: 1700000000132-enforce-explicit-postgres-context.
- Migration: 1700000000133-add-cloud-email-passkeys.
- The owner verifies the exact 0132 ledger and policy before applying 0133. The new pending-signup and passkey tables have no tenant membership side effects. The down migration refuses to remove populated passkey credentials.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- Email verification establishes address control, while a verified passkey assertion authenticates the account. Matching email addresses never merge existing accounts or grant tenant membership.
- Use SimpleWebAuthn server 13.3.2 to include the attestation certificate trust-anchor verification fix for GHSA-6hxq-p678-4hr2.

## Known limitations

- Lost-passkey recovery requires a separate verified support process until a recovery method is deliberately introduced.

## Rollback

- Roll the application back only to the signed compatibility release while retaining the 0133 schema. Do not remove populated passkey tables or strand passkey-only accounts; provide a verified alternate sign-in before disabling this method.

## Validation evidence

- Focused signup, passkey, and Cloud-session tests; PostgreSQL owner/preflight, authorization, cross-database portability, and browser acceptance remain release gates.
